title: 2026 NHL Selke Trophy finalists: Will it be Suzuki, or a different first-time winner?
content:
Anthony Cirelli of the Tampa Bay Lightning, Brock Nelson of the Colorado Avalanche and Nick Suzuki of the Montreal Canadiens are the finalists for the Frank J. Selke Trophy, awarded to the forward who best excels in the defensive aspects of the game, the NHL revealed on Friday.

The award is voted upon by members of the Pro Hockey Writers’ Association, and the winner will be announced next month. In 2024-25, Florida Panthers center Aleksander Barkov won for the second straight season and the third time overall. He tore his ACL and MCL in training camp, though, opening the door for a first-timer to take home the trophy this year.

Cirelli, long the Lightning’s defensive lynchpin up front, has passed some of his defensive workload to teammate Yanni Gourde, but Tampa Bay still won Cirelli’s minutes by a stunning 60-29 ratio. He also was a finalist last year, along with Barkov and Florida’s Sam Bennett.

Nelson is thriving in a significant role in all situations for the Avalanche, this season’s Presidents’ Trophy winners who hold a 2-0 second-round series lead over Minnesota. Nelson was traded from the New York Islanders last season and signed a three-year, $22.5 million extension with the Avalanche last summer. He would be the first Avalanche player to win the Selke.

Suzuki, considered the favorite to win, recorded the highest Defensive Rating among the finalists. He excelled against elite competition on both sides of the puck, and in the regular season, the Canadiens won his five-on-five minutes 72-39. Suzuki’s production also likely gives him a leg up. He finished with 101 points, a career best, and led the way on a young Montreal team that took another enormous step forward. If there’s a knock against him, it’s that he played the fewest short-handed minutes among the finalists.

The Selke Trophy was first awarded in 1978 to Bob Gainey of the Canadiens, a Hockey Hall of Famer who would go on to win it three more times consecutively.
